newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.S. files again for WTO panel in EU grains row.
newsitem.headline: U.S. files again for WTO panel in EU grains row.

text.p: The United States has withdrawn a request filed in February and renewed last month for a World Trade Organisation (WTO) panel in its grains dispute with the European Union, trade sources said.
But they said Washington had put in a new panel request which will be on the agenda for a meeting of the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) on Thursday.

The switch means a panel will not be created automatically at the April 10 session, as it would have been if the original U.S. application had been maintained, since the EU is almost certain to block the request.
But if Washington persists, a panel will be set up the next time the DSB meets, probably in early May.
It was the latest turnaround in the dispute, which dates back two years, over EU grain tariffs on wheat, rye, barley, sorghum and rice which Washington says violate WTO accords.
Last month the EU said it would introduce a new rice import system and a new tariff quota for U.S. malting barley, which U.S. officials indicated met most of their concerns.
But Brussels voiced anger when the U.S. renewed its panel request on March 26, warning that the move could backfire and lead the EU to drop the planned changes.
Diplomats said the latest U.S. move appeared designed to remove the immediate prospect of creation of a panel but to maintain pressure on the EU to go ahead with the measures.
